description:
KFT's own §11 'Open questions' (fine-tuning.md ~line 481), folded only on the next pressure break, never speculatively (each note says 'unless a pressure test forces it into the contract'; ROADMAP.md Phase F6): (1) adapter-selection hint — whether the job manifest may carry an engine hint or it stays producer-internal (§9); (2) multi-node / distributed runs — cost metering + checkpoint lineage across GPUs (§5.3/§6), where the cost unit + checkpoint-asset shape must not preclude it; (3) resume-checkpoint ref — confirm the job manifest carries a resume checkpoint ref cleanly (a run based_on a prior finetuned model, §5 lineage); (4) eval-as-reward — how tightly method:dpo binds to a KCS scenario as its reward (§6.1) and whether reward scenarios need a distinct KCS profile. (Item 5, capability versioning, is resolved by Phase F2 / chief/54.) PARKED: reactive by design; authored and held. KFT is candidate (0.4.0). Public-safe: bind roles.

**Unparked 2026-08-25 by operator decision.** The reactive-by-design discipline said to wait for a pressure test to force the question. US-1 IS that pressure test, and it is constructible today — so waiting was waiting for someone to do the work this tasklist describes. The trade is deliberate and worth stating: a manufactured pressure leg can force a question no real user has, so **US-2 folds a clause only if US-1 finds a CONCRETE break.** A leg that finds none closes the question as 'pressure applied, no break found', which is a real answer and a better one than an open note that never resolves.

userStories.title: New KFT pressure-test leg forcing the open question
userStories.description: Add the scenario leg that FORCES whichever §11 question demands an answer, before folding — KFT folds each open question only under pressure (each note is explicit).
acceptanceCriteria: A scenarios/ leg (extending scenarios/e2e-finetune.md / e2e-finetune-multimodal.md / e2e-producer-exhaust-finetune.md, or a new focused scenario) forces one §11 question: adapter-selection hint (§11.1), distributed-run cost metering + checkpoint lineage (§11.2), resume-checkpoint ref (§11.3), or eval-as-reward KCS profile for method:dpo (§11.4).
The leg is adversarial and shows the concrete break that forces a contract answer; only the forced question is carried into US-2.
It uses the KINP §3.4 placeholder namespaces and names no product.
userStories.notes: scenarios/kft-resume-checkpoint.md added — focused adversarial leg forcing KFT §11.3 only. Step 1 confirms the warm-start half HELD (base_model takes a finetuned model entity; lineage, §5.4 inheritance and §5.1.1 publication all compose transitively). The resume half broke five ways: FT-R (high/structural — no slot names a checkpoint; schema is additionalProperties:false; FT-C's reproducibility anchor stops determining the run), FT-S (high/gate — the only permissive slot hyperparams is read by no normative clause, and §5.4 leaves a mid-run checkpoint with no egress class, so a continued-pre-training resume cloud-places weights that memorized a local-only corpus), FT-T (high — activity identity: no continues/resumes relation, retrains means re-train-from-scratch), FT-U (high — §6's job+step idempotency collides on re-executed steps), FT-V (med — FT-E's estimate cannot net out completed steps). Blocking FT-R, FT-S. Closing section states §11.1/§11.2/§11.4/§11.6 are untouched by construction. Placeholder namespaces only (refkb/mediastore/orchestrator/provider), no product named. Verification: node scripts/check-doc-integrity.mjs green (44 markdown files, 752 relative links, 0 errors, 3 status tables match); check-schemas OK (9 schemas, 274 positions, 78 $refs, 3 fixtures); check-registry OK (27 relation names); check-tasklist-categories OK (7 tasklists); .chief/verify.sh: all selected gates green — allowing merge. Note: doc-integrity was red with 9 PRE-EXISTING dangling links to tasks/chief/53-multi-authority-scenario.json (retired into completed/) — confirmed identical on a clean baseline — and verify.sh path-selects that guard from any changed doc, so it blocked this branch; repointed in a separate commit, link target only.

userStories.notes: KFT 0.5.0 -> 0.6.0, Status Candidate. Folded FT-R...FT-V from scenarios/kft-resume-checkpoint.md, additively. NEW NORMATIVE §3.4 (optional top-level `resume` {checkpoint, of_job, at_step}: a pinned input entering §5.2 used[] so FT-C's anchor holds; the ONLY slot for a resume ref, one in the permissive `hyperparams` is refused `invalid`; never corpus). §4.2 effective egress over {data u base u resume.checkpoint}; §4.3 union license/tier likewise. §5.4 binds a mid-run checkpoint's class AT PUBLICATION (the hole that existed independently of resume, on §6's subscribe stream). §5.2 makes a continuation leg a NEW activity linked by the new core relation `continues` (registry/relations.tsv, distinct from retrains/supersedes). §6 keeps job+step idempotency sound, `step` counts from the root leg, NORMATIVE curve-join rule + optional non-authoritative `attempt`. §7 estimates the REMAINDER with at_step verified against prior provenance, against the ceiling net of cumulative spent_units across the chain. §3.3.1 gating set + §3.3.2 two rows + a fifth normative consequence. §11.3 marked RESOLVED IN PLACE (numbering deliberately unshifted, like §11.5); §11.1/§11.2/§11.4/§11.6 stay open; item 5 already resolved by ADR-0009/KCB §7 (chief/54) and restated as such. Schema in lockstep: `resume` object, additionalProperties:false, NOT in `required` -> every 0.4.0/0.5.0 manifest still validates; golden fixture schemas/fixtures/finetune-job.json exercises it (one-fixture-per-schema is enforced by check-schemas, so a second fixture is not expressible). Placeholder CURIEs only, no product named. Changelog entry + Pressure test section cite the leg and record the second, narrow gate. All four status mirrors updated (README, specs/README x2, ECOSYSTEM, plus the unchecked CLAUDE.md prose).
